label: accepted

evidence.V1: The doorway reads at a glance in front, three-quarter and silhouette (centred rectangular opening in a block wall); the top view is the expected slab.
evidence.V2: Clear tiers: wall and cap (big), jamb blocks, lintel blocks and door frame (medium), gold keystone and threshold (small).
evidence.V3: Proportions are sensible but plain: a thin flat-faced frame, square lintel blocks and a tiny keystone; it reads as stiff primitives more than a confident stylised doorway.
evidence.V4: Even chamfers on the blocks, cap, frame and keystone catch light consistently (close_lintel_studio, close_end_section_studio).
evidence.V5: Close-ups are clean; no pinches, z-fighting or stray facets on the frame, lintel or threshold.
evidence.V6: Stone in three values plus one gold keystone accent; disciplined across colourways.
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material, chamfered stone and a gold keystone per the modular kit rules.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Default keeps the doorway walkable, CanTouch off, white MeshPart, grid-corner pivot; T1 tiling passes.

top_fixes: Make the door surround bolder: a thicker frame with a stepped or arched lintel and a larger, more prominent keystone
Vary the jamb block sizes (alternating quoins) so the coursing is less grid-like
Add a slight cap overhang and drip shadow, and give the threshold a raised step lip
